project: Kikar Hamedina Towers (מגדלי כיכר המדינה), Tel Aviv
audience: Acheteurs français et belges, souvent en préparation d'alyah ou à la recherche d'un pied-à-terre ; olim francophones déjà en Israël qui montent en gamme. Ils achètent à distance et comparent en shekels.
names: Nom principal : les tours Kikar Hamedina. Première mention : « les tours Kikar Hamedina (Kikar Hamedina Towers, מגדלי כיכר המדינה) ». À placer naturellement : « Kikar Hamedina à Tel Aviv », « la place Kikar Hamedina » (une fois : « la place de l’État »), « rue He Be’Iyar ». Une fois : « les tours en spirale ». Tours A, B et C. Constructeurs : Electra Construction et Ashtrom. Architectes : Yaski Mor Sivan Architectes. Propriétaires : les propriétaires fonciers / la société des propriétaires fonciers. Jamais « promoteur ».
related_searches: « tours » seul se lit comme « visites » : toujours « tours Kikar Hamedina » avec « appartements » ou « prix » à côté. PAA : « Quel est le quartier le plus chic de Tel Aviv ? »

claims.claim: Name: Kikar Hamedina Towers (מגדלי כיכר המדינה); also called the Spiral Towers (מגדלי הספירלה).

The three towers stand inside the round Kikar Hamedina square in north Tel Aviv, ringed by He Be'Iyar street; Weizmann Street meets the square from the south and Jabotinsky Street from the east. The municipality's neighbourhood name: 'the New North, Kikar Hamedina area' (הצפון החדש - סביבת כיכר המדינה).
Three residential towers: two of 40 floors and one of 37 floors (tower B).
claims.conflict: The city's buildings layer lists all three at 40 floors, and its permit record notes a request for 2 more floors in tower B. Older reports say 42 floors.
claims.write_as: 40, 40 and 37 floors. Optionally: a request for 2 more floors in tower B was recorded. Never 42.

claims.claim: 453 apartments in all; about 150 m² per apartment on average.
Each floor is turned 1.25 degrees relative to the floor below; over 40 floors the turn adds up to about 50 degrees (about 46 degrees over 37 floors).
claims.conflict: One supplier case study says 2.5 degrees: never use it.

claims.claim: The apartments belong to about 250 rights holders, the heirs of private investors who bought the plots in 1942; they formed an association in 1997 that became the landowners' company. The rights holders received the apartments in exchange for the land; the order of choice was set by a lottery.
claims.write_as: 'about 250 rights holders'. Never the word 'developer' (יזם): 'the landowners' / 'the landowners' company'.

claims.claim: Milestones: excavation and shoring permit 12.2018; building permit 12.2022; first concrete pour 18.12.2022; the city's building-site record lists the stage 'frame completed' (גמר שלד) as of 23.4.2026.
A public park of about 40 dunam (about 4 hectares) at the heart of the square.
The three deals' range is ₪9.58M to ₪10.63M; their average about ₪9.93M, about ₪71,000/m² (derived).
The building-permit addresses of the towers: He Be'Iyar 25, 45 and 65.
Height: about 160 m for towers A and C and about 157 m for tower B.
claims.conflict: Other lists give 156 m or 153 m.
claims.write_as: 'about 160 m' (the conservative wording: 'up to about 160 m').

claims.claim: Architects: Yaski Mor Sivan Architects (MYS), chosen in a competition in 2000.
Builders: Electra Construction and Ashtrom, jointly, under a construction contract of about ₪1.4 billion (₪700 million each); they were chosen in November 2021 from six bidding groups.
Project management: Waxman Govrin Geva (WXG), with the project since 2001. Landscape architecture: T.M.A.
Financing: Bareket Capital with Clal and Migdal, credit of about ₪2.05 billion.
On one of the basement levels: a swimming pool, a gym, a spa, treatment rooms and multi-purpose halls. The city's building-site record lists a spa, a pool of 290 m³ and a gym in the basements.
Parking: about 1,620 underground spaces on 3 levels; about 906 of them private for the apartment owners and about 720 public (14 for disabled drivers).
claims.conflict: 1,626 = 906 + 720 in one 2026 report; 4 levels in a 2015 plan.

claims.claim: Occupancy: the published estimates range from 2026 to 2028. The builders' published dates are 2026 and April 2027; a 9.2025 estimate by the project's financier spoke of 'within about two years' (about 2027); a 4.2025 report said the end of 2028. No official occupancy date (Form 4) has been published.
claims.write_as: Give the range 2026-2028 and the most recent estimates without naming who said them by name (roles are fine: 'the builders', 'the financier'). Never one date as fact. For a given apartment, the delivery date is the one in the seller's contract.

claims.claim: Where each tower stands on the plot: tower A to the south-west, tower B to the south-east, tower C to the north-east (about 75-78 m from the plot centre).

The architects' concept: each residential floor steps back slightly from the floor below and turns in a circular movement inspired by the round shape of the square; the façades are a modern reading of the ring's buildings: floor slabs and white curtain walls.

The façade: floor-to-ceiling glass and white aluminium curtain walls, insulated glass with built-in electric shading, aluminium-and-glass shading fins 300 mm deep, full-height pivot windows with inner railings.

What lies in each direction (straight-line distances from the plot; what a given apartment sees depends on its tower, floor and direction and was not published): the Mediterranean, nearest waterline about 2 km to the north-west; the Tel Aviv port about 1.9 km north-west; Ramat Aviv about 2.5 km north and Tel Aviv University about 3.2 km north-north-east; Park HaYarkon to the north and north-east; Azrieli towers about 1.4 km south; Azrieli Sarona about 1.6 km south; Ichilov about 0.7 km south; City Hall and Rabin Square about 1 km south-west; Habima about 1.9 km south-west; the Ayalon and the Savidor station about 0.8 km east.
A published listing on a high floor describes a north-west sea view.
A published penthouse listing: 258 m² inside and 57 m² outside, 4 bedrooms, 3.5 bathrooms, views to the north, west and south, 2 parking spaces.
15 high-speed lifts (4 to 6 metres a second) serve the apartments.
The average deal in the towers is about ₪65,000/m²; on the high floors and in the penthouses ₪80,000 to ₪150,000/m².

No official unit mix or floor plans have been published; apartments per floor were not published. Apartment sizes seen in published deals and listings: 4 rooms of 132, 134, 140 and 148 m²; 5 rooms of 154 m²; 4 rooms of 168 m² (planned as 5); 170 m² and 200 m² units; a penthouse of 258 m² with 57 m² outdoor (a 42 m² terrace and a 15 m² balcony).
claims.write_as: Write as 'sizes that appeared in published deals and listings', not as a mix.

claims.claim: Listings describe the towers as 4 and 5 rooms (living room plus 3-4 bedrooms) with penthouses on top.
Balconies in published listings: about 12 to 15.5 m² (154 m² + 12; 134 m² + 14; 168 m² + about 14.5; 132 m² + about 15.5).

Specification items that listings advertise (advertised, not an official specification): fishbone parquet, designer marble, VRF air conditioning, central heating, a safe room (mamad) with a full bathroom, a smart-home system, high ceilings, security 24/7.
Listings show two parking spaces and a storage room with a typical apartment; one listing offers 4 parking spaces and 2 storage rooms.
The lobby: listings describe a lobby with a security guard.
Air conditioning: a Daikin VRF system (central multi-split).

Low asking prices of about ₪6.25-6.3M appeared for the RIGHTS to an apartment (for example 134 m² on floor 23, 12.2024; 154 m² on floor 4); one such listing says the buyer still pays the construction cost, about ₪28,000 per m². So a rights price and a finished-apartment price are not comparable.
claims.write_as: Explain the difference; never present ₪6.3M as the price of an apartment.

claims.claim: A dedicated internal access road serves school drop-off at set hours.
The project's own commerce is a few small café kiosks in the park (no shopping mall); the shops stay in the square's ring.
Garbage chutes and entrance doors are supplied by Rav Bariach.

A new state primary school inside the square (the north building of the public plot): 18 classes plus 6 special-education classes, with an underground sports hall and a sunken courtyard; it opened with the start of a school year (reported 24.9.2026). The city's 2026-27 schools list places two schools at He Be'Iyar 75: the Kikar Hamedina primary school and the Meir Shalev middle school.
A 750 m running track; a wide perimeter boulevard with a bike path, three rows of trees, kiosks and shaded seating; lawns, playgrounds, a dog garden, game tables.

Three published deals in the towers, all 4 rooms of 140 m² on floors 38-39: ₪10.63M on floor 38 (12.2024, about ₪75,900/m²); ₪9.59M on floor 39 (5.2024, about ₪68,500/m²); ₪9.58M on floor 38 (4.2024, about ₪68,400/m²). Which tower each was in was not published.

Asking prices published (asking, not deals): a penthouse on floor 39, 258 m² + 57 m² outdoor: ₪43M (about ₪150,000/m², ~1.2025-4.2025); floor 35, 154 m² + 12 m² balcony, south-east: ₪14.5M; a high floor, 4 rooms of 168 m² + about 14.5 m², north-west sea view: ₪13.7M (1.2026); floor 12, 148 m²: ₪10.3M (4.2025); floor 16, 4 rooms of 132 m² + about 15.5 m²: ₪10M.

Around the square: most apartments sold in the past year went for ₪63,000-66,000/m² (official deal records, 4.2026); the New North / Kikar Hamedina neighbourhood averaged ₪67,747/m² for 3-room deals (7.2025), the 8th most expensive in Tel Aviv; 148 apartments sold there in a year at an average of ₪68,000/m² and ₪5.66M per deal (data to 6.2024).

Purchase tax for an Israeli resident buying a single (only) apartment: 0% up to ₪1,978,745; 3.5% up to ₪2,347,040; 5% up to ₪6,055,070; 8% up to ₪20,183,565; 10% above. The amounts updated 16.1.2024 were frozen by law, so they apply in 2026.
Purchase tax on an additional apartment, and for a foreign resident: 8% up to ₪6,055,070 and 10% above.
Example (derived), a ₪10,000,000 apartment: about ₪514,000 of purchase tax for an Israeli buying a single apartment; about ₪879,000 for an additional apartment or a foreign resident.
New immigrants (olim) have a reduced purchase-tax track under conditions set by law; check it with a tax advisor.

Mortgage limits (Bank of Israel, since 11.2012): up to 75% of the value for a first (single) home, up to 70% for a replacement home, up to 50% for an additional / investment apartment and for a non-resident buyer.
Example (derived), a ₪10,000,000 apartment: own equity of at least ₪2.5M with a 75% mortgage, ₪3M at 70%, ₪5M at 50%.
A real-estate broker is entitled to a fee only if licensed, holding a signed written order from the client, and the effective cause of the deal; the fee is what the written order says.
There is no sales office and no price list: the apartments are resold by their owners, usually through real-estate brokers.
At most 200 to 250 apartments are expected to be offered for sale, because many owners plan to live in the towers (a 4.2025 report).
Rentals in the towers start only after occupancy; no rent has been published for the towers.
claims.write_as: Never give a rent figure for the towers.

claims.claim: Construction method: the circular cores rose with imported slip forms, about 1.5 m a working day, which is 5 to 7 floors a month per tower; about 7 floors a month against about 3 in conventional building.
All three towers are built at the same time, not in phases.
Foundations: about 300,000 m³ of earth excavated; three reinforced rafts on piles.
The public works in the square (park, ring street He Be'Iyar) are expected to be completed by the end of 2027 (the municipality's project director, 9.2026). This is the PUBLIC works, not the towers.

Timeline anchors: 1942 plots bought; 1997 owners' association; 2000 architects chosen; 24.6.2013 the plan in force; 3.2018 the traffic amendment of the plan in force; 11.2021 builders chosen; 12.2022 building permit and first pour; 4.2026 frame completed.
Its plan of 1969 was drawn with Oscar Niemeyer; Israel Lotan and Abba Elhanani designed the ring buildings, built mostly in the early 1970s. The circle first appeared in a 1939 city plan.
The plan for the compound (in force since 24.6.2013) allows 453 housing units, about 59,175 m² of housing and 6,000 m² of public buildings; the plan area is about 78 dunam (77.743).
An ecological pond 1 m deep with perennial planting, flow channels, bridges and paths.
claims.conflict: The pond's area: 3.5 or 8 dunam in older plans.
claims.write_as: Give the depth, never the area.

claims.claim: 560 new trees planted and 36 existing trees kept.
Public works of about ₪150 million.
A community centre in the south building of the public plot: activity rooms, a dance studio, a multi-purpose hall, an urban lounge and open courtyards; a café of about 60 m².
The school and the community centre flank an open walk that continues Jabotinsky Street into the park, on the west side of the square.
Green places within 2-4 minutes: Gan Avraham, Biltmore garden, Pollak garden; a dog park in Lisin grove (4 minutes).
Kikar Hamedina is described as the largest square in Israel and the largest plaza in Tel Aviv.
In the 1950s and 1960s a circus (Medrano) pitched its tent in the sandy centre; on 3.9.2011 about 300,000 people gathered there in the March of the Million, the peak of the social-justice protests.

The ring is Tel Aviv's luxury-fashion address. Houses named in a public list: Gucci, Saint Laurent, Givenchy, Dior, Valentino, Chloé, Burberry, Fendi, Dolce & Gabbana. Gucci reopened a new store in the ring (reported 1.2025); a watch and jewellery lounge of about 250 m² opened in 12.2025.
claims.write_as: Shops change: say 'among the houses on the ring' and never promise a specific store today.

claims.claim: Cafés and food on the ring, a minute's walk: Bakery Kikar Hamedina, Lechem Erez, Nuchi, Open, Nespresso; supermarkets City Market and Victory; a Super-Pharm pharmacy on Weizmann.
About 13,300 people live near the square, in about 6,000 households (2023 municipal data).

The ring around the towers is being renewed too: 16 other building sites within 250 m, most of them urban-renewal rebuilds of 7 to 9 floors; wider sidewalks, a circular bike path and four new pedestrian and cycle crossings.
Light rail Purple Line: Ichilov station about 350 m away, about 2 minutes' walk; planned to open in 2028.
Light rail Red Line: Arlozorov station about 860 m away, about 11 minutes' walk; running since 18.8.2023.
Tel Aviv Savidor Center railway station: about 850 m, about 9 minutes' walk.
Light rail Green Line on Ibn Gabirol: Arlozorov station about 730 m, about 9 minutes' walk; planned for 2030 in full (southern section 2028).
53 bus lines stop within 5 minutes' walk of the ring, 95 within 10 minutes (a normal weekday, 8.9.2026).
Roads: Weizmann about 140 m, Namir Road about 530 m, Ibn Gabirol about 720 m, the Ayalon Highway about 800 m.
Ichilov (Tel Aviv Sourasky) Medical Center: about 0.7-0.85 km, about 9 minutes' walk.
Park HaYarkon: its nearest edge about 1 km north, about 13 minutes' walk; Sportek about 22 minutes.
claims.conflict: An old report says 200 m: never use it.

claims.claim: Schools and kindergartens: the new primary school inside the square (1 minute); Ahavat Zion primary (3 minutes); Herzliya Hebrew Gymnasium (4 minutes, about 400 m); a municipal kindergarten 1 minute away; several kindergartens on Lisin Street 4 minutes away.
claims.write_as: Registration zones are set by the city every year: never promise a school place.

claims.claim: Health: a Clalit clinic 4 minutes; pharmacies 1-3 minutes.
Culture: Beit Hahayal theatre 6 minutes; the Tel Aviv Museum of Art about 14 minutes; the Arlozorov 97 community country club 5 minutes; synagogues from 1 minute (Weizmann 71).
Neighbourhood prices and character are those of north Tel Aviv: Ibn Gabirol, Yehuda HaMaccabi, Arlozorov and the Tzameret towers around; Ichilov within walking distance.
The plot of the towers is about 28 dunam of residential land (lot 101, about 28,380 m²); 13.8 dunam on the west of the square hold the school and the community centre.
